text:
Predicates:
RankedHighly(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is one of the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
IgaŚwiątek(y) ::: y is Iga Świątek.
RolandGarros2022(x) ::: x is a player at Roland Garros 2022.
Female(x) ::: x is female.
Male(x) ::: x is male.
CocoGauff(x) ::: x is Coco Gauff.
RafaelNadal(x) ::: x is Rafael Nadal.

Premises:
∀x (RankedHighly(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If someone is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association, then they are one of the most active players in major tennis.
∀x (LostTo(x, IgaŚwiątek) → RankedHighly(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek at Roland Garros 2022 is ranked highly.
∀x (RolandGarros2022(x) ∧ Female(x)) → LostTo(x, IgaŚwiątek) ::: All female tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
∀x (RolandGarros2022(x)) → (Female(x) ∨ Male(x)) ::: All tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 are either female or male.
∀x (Male(x) ∧ RolandGarros2022(x)) → LostTo(x, RafaelNadal) ::: All male tennis players at Roland Garros in 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
( (RankedHighly(CocoGauff) ∨ LostTo(CocoGauff, RafaelNadal)) ) → ¬Male(CocoGauff) ::: If Coco Gauff is ranked highly or lost to Rafael Nadal, then she is not a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
CocoGauff(CocoGauff) ::: Coco Gauff is at Roland Garros 2022.

Conclusion:
RankedHighly(CocoGauff) ∧ ActivePlayer(CocoGauff) ::: Coco Gauff is among the most active major tennis players.
